claims.text: Conventional single-phase ZrB2 typically requires temperatures above 2300 °C for densification.
Conventional single-phase ZrB2 has inadequate oxidation resistance in high-temperature environments.
Conventional single-phase ZrB2 has inadequate corrosion resistance in liquid plating-metal environments.
Replacing 5–10% of the Zr sublattice with Hf and applying reactive SPS at 1600–1700 °C will form a homogeneous (Zr,Hf)B2 solid solution.
The proposed Hf substitution and SPS treatment will refine the grain boundaries.
The modified material will develop continuous HfO2 interfacial passivation layers during service.
Hf substitution reduces the activation energy for densification during sintering.
The reduction in densification activation energy permits full densification at or below 1700 °C.
Hf preferentially oxidizes during high-temperature oxidation and liquid-metal plating service.
Preferential oxidation of Hf produces a robust HfO2 passivation layer.
The HfO2 layer acts as a diffusion barrier that slows oxygen ingress.
The HfO2 layer mitigates liquid-metal-induced corrosion.
The proposed material will have greater mechanical strength than both high-temperature-sintered pure ZrB2 and prior lower-temperature specimens.
The proposed material will have greater oxidation resistance than both high-temperature-sintered pure ZrB2 and prior lower-temperature specimens.
The proposed material will have greater liquid plating-metal corrosion resistance than both high-temperature-sintered pure ZrB2 and prior lower-temperature specimens.
Maintaining processing temperatures at or below 1700 °C is necessary for the proposed lower-temperature manufacturing advantage.
Processing outside the proposed parameters may impair formation or effectiveness of the HfO2 layer.
